approximationNotes: Two broadside images do not metrically determine hidden thickness or internal bolt geometry.

Strict CS2 silhouette target 0.90 is not yet met; the current front/back masks are 0.8101/0.7985. The source-fit magazine envelope is retained while the receiver-parented bolt and muzzle-side barrel band are locked.

Scope loop 12 adds source-sized machined collars over the two coaxial torus rings, preserves clamp tops/saddles/rail mounts, and measures each ring against the actual scope tube mesh rather than the containing scope group. The broadside hardware is still less detailed than the source.

The crown decal now conforms to the objective bell in both x taper and y circular section, uses a 0.0015-unit surface offset, and is enlarged 1.08x. The source gold/skull pixels are clearer and attached in orbit, but remain softer than the reference foil mark.

Loop 13 shortens and widens the rounded trigger guard while retaining its receiver socket and trigger pivot; the comparison is closer in height but the lower trigger/magazine assembly remains compact.

Loop 14 replaces the visually thin spring with a continuous 18-turn tube helix at 0.017 radius and 0.052 radial amplitude, adds machined collars on both front/back spring seats, and keeps the spine/telescoping tubes/feet attached. The spring now reads as a coil from broadside and muzzle orbit, though hidden-side detail remains inferred.

Loop 15 tested a vertical-only magazine enlargement while preserving the accepted X station; it reduced front IoU from 0.8101 to 0.8076 and was rolled back. The source-fit compact magazine envelope is intentionally retained pending stronger evidence.

The attachment gate now uses actual shell/child meshes for receiver, bolt shroud, trigger guard, magazine, bipod saddle, scope tube, crown projection, barrel, and muzzle. Parent-group containment is no longer accepted as seam evidence.
Medusa paint is a shell-only curved projection from supplied pixels; it is not used as structural geometry.
The thumbhole is a real extruded stock cut with a projection cutout; hidden thickness and interior hardware remain inferred.
